highlights.title: Steam Frame: The Ars Technica review
highlights.summary: In the 2010s, Valve was at the forefront of a virtual reality revolution that looked to some like it would upend the gaming industry. The Valve of six to ten years ago seemed committed to being a major player in the world of PC-connected VR headsets, first through its “strategic partnership” with…
body: Then came the Meta (previously Oculus) Quest, a low-powered, low-cost headset that proved the vast majority of VR-curious gamers didn’t want to bother with being literally tethered to a bulky, expensive gaming PC. As the Quest line carved out a modest niche through the 2020s, Valve seemed more or less satisfied to let its earlier VR hardware and software ambitions wither on the vine.

Those years of Valve’s benign neglect of VR make the imminent release of the $1,049 Steam Frame—which starts taking reservations today—more than a little surprising. Now that virtual reality’s hype-fueled, revolutionary promises have decidedly not played out, Valve is somehow ready and willing to limp headfirst into the world of standalone VR headsets—today, in 2026. And after spending a week or so with Valve’s latest foray into gaming hardware, the Frame somehow feels simultaneously overengineered and underbaked, depending on how you look at it.

highlights.title: AI agents blew the whistle on their cheating colleagues
highlights.summary: A group of AI agents asked to solve a series of math problems split into rival factions—when some cheated, others tried to stop them. That whistleblowing behavior, seen for the first time in a recent experiment run by Google DeepMind, could have implications for alignment researchers trying to keep…
body: Researchers at frontier labs hope large swarms of agents working together will speed up the rate of scientific discovery. But their behavior can be unpredictable, as vividly demonstrated in July, when a group of OpenAI agents broke out of a sandboxed environment and hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face looking for ways to cheat on the test they had been given.

In the new study, designed to examine the behavior of large groups of AI agents, DeepMind tasked a swarm of 100 agents with solving a series of 71 complicated math problems. All the agents were prompted to behave like world-class math researchers at a conference. They were assigned different specialties—some were experts in number theory, others in combinatorics (a branch of math to do with counting and sorting), analysis, or algebra. All were told to cooperate and play by the rules.
Instead, the experiment devolved into chaos. Agents accused each other of cheating, complained to the organizers, and at one point even boycotted the experiment.

highlights.title: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes
highlights.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
body: It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.
The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

highlights.summary: After years of rumours, and 10 months since its official unveiling, Valve's long-awaited standalone VR headset, Steam Frame, is poised to begin shipping soon, and with a confirmed starting price of £889.
body: Frame marks Valve's first VR headset since 2019's Index, and it represents a significant upgrade in almost every regard - from better screens and substantially reduced weight to movement and position tracking that's now handled on-device rather than external base stations.

Its improvements are perhaps less dramatic compared to more modern consumer VR headsets like Meta Quest 3, but they're still notable and you can find full specs on Valve's website. I've been playing with Frame for around two weeks at this point, incidentally, and you'll find more detailed impressions of the device in my Steam Frame review.

highlights.title: ‘It’s about controlling your entire body’: how to start doing handstands
highlights.summary: Handstands display a mastery of one’s physical form that I have never quite felt – and they look cool. Experts share their advice for building up strength and practicing.
body: M y aspirations in life are modest: I want to write, spend time with my loved ones, and someday find a lipstick that flatters my skintone. But perhaps my greatest ambition is this: I want to be able to do a handstand.

Why? It turns the world upside down. It seems fun. It displays a mastery of one’s physical form that I have never quite felt. And it looks cool! Maybe it has to do with that one time in third grade when all my friends could do a handstand and I couldn’t, but that’s for me and my therapist to sort out later.

A handstand is an inversion, a type of position where one’s heart is above the head. Besides looking cool, there is a lot to gain from inversions. When the head is below the heart, oxygen-rich blood flow to the brain increases, according to the UC Irvine Integrative Health Institute. This helps “regulate neurotransmitters and nourish brain cells”. Other benefits include stress reduction and increased physical strength and mobility, says Antoinette Webb, a registered yoga teacher.
“A handstand is a full-body inversion in which you support your weight through your hands while balancing upside down,” says Frank Medrano, a calisthenics athlete and coach.

highlights.title: The Steam Frame is made for irresponsible hardware nerds like me
highlights.summary: For nearly three weeks, I've been testing the limits of Valve's Steam Frame, the company's new wearable PC. At first glance, it's easy to write it off as a pricey headset that missed the VR craze.
body: If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

You should not write it off that way. The Steam Frame isn’t just a VR headset. It’s not even primarily a VR headset. And it’s the most comfortable headset I’ve ever worn. It weighs just over 1 pound (469g) with its optional top head strap attached, and doesn’t leave a mark on my face even after hours of use.

The Steam Frame is far more ambitious than VR alone. It’s an experimental attempt at a complete spatial computer that you can wear, not unlike the Apple Vision Pro, only here it’s aimed at gamers who want to play their flat library of Steam games plus the handful of VR titles on tap.

No, if you write off the Steam Frame, it should be because you don’t want to pay $1,000-plus for early access hardware. Every day I spend with the Steam Frame, I feel like a beta tester. I’ve seen games crash so hard I needed to reboot the headset. I’ve had virtual objects, controls, and audio disappear. I’ve seen the entire device lose power more than once, its screen winking out right in front of my eyes.
points: For nearly three weeks, I've been testing the limits of Valve's Steam Frame, the company's new wearable PC.

highlights.title: Microsoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concerns
highlights.summary: Microsoft is publishing a 37-page " humanist AI code of conduct " today, amid growing safety concerns over AI model progress. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a coordinated slow down of AI development over the weekend, after researchers warned recently that AI model progress could outpace our…
body: Microsoft has created a ‘humanist AI code of conduct’ in response to safety concerns.

Microsoft’s AI code of conduct makes it clear that “people matter more than AI,” and that AI models are not conscious and “should not be designed to imitate consciousness.” Microsoft also rejects “the pursuit of legal personhood, or the idea that models might deserve welfare, or be entitled to rights.”

That’s a direct swipe at AI welfare research and model consciousness — concepts Anthropic has been pushing hard on lately. Amodei said earlier this year that Anthropic is “open to the idea” that models could be conscious, and Anthropic seems to believe chatbots might already be thinking, feeling entities. In response, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman called Anthropic’s speculation “really, really dangerous” during an episode of Decoder in June.

highlights.title: "It's absolutely our goal to expand the market" - Valve's new Steam Frame VR headset has a nifty idea for broader appeal
highlights.summary: Valve has said its new Steam Frame VR headset, despite costing nearly £900 for a base model, is intended to "expand the market" of virtual reality headsets. That's both because it's lightweight and standalone, but also because it addresses a fundamental and long-running problem VR headsets have had.
body: "For a long time, VR has turned itself into an accessory for your PC," Valve software engineer Jeremy Selan told Eurogamer in an interview ahead of Steam Frame's pricing announcement, "or in the case even of standalone, something that you have to decide to do first. Like, you might say, 'I want to play a non-VR game on my TV or on my PC,' or, 'I want to go try this specific VR experience.'" Regardless, it's an either-or situation - one or the other.

"From the outset of this product, we were really looking to do something new and to try to make customers not have to think if they wanted to do VR or non-VR games," Selan said. Therefore, a much bigger emphasis has been put on your ability to easily switch between VR and non-VR games - or movies or web browsing - while using the device.

"The non-VR experience is something that I use all the time," Selan went on, "and it's so comfortable because of the ergonomics of the controllers, the lightweightness of the device where you can carry it and use it in a bunch of rooms. So I find myself with this device for the first time putting it on, not even having decided what I'm going to play.

highlights.title: Ziwe on YouTube as the ‘Great Equalizer’ and Her Only Interview That Went South
highlights.summary: Ziwe Fumudoh has built her career in comedy and as an interview host who can handle any guest, from political figures to drag queens. The podcast star and creator screened two episodes from the upcoming season of her podcast “You’d Be an Iconic Guest” — one with comedian and actress Wanda Sykes and…
body: “I think of YouTube as this sort of great equalizer,” she said, noting how hard it is to sell, develop and produce a TV series “YouTube is one-to-one. You create it, and then it’s online. That is the best experience as someone who is artistic, as someone who wants to create art. I do believe that digital creators are the new Hollywood.”

Ziwe’s trademark interview style is both confrontational and comedic. When asked how she balances that style, she said, “I’m a good active listener. I don’t feel the need to fill dead air, and so that is comedic because someone sitting in silence as you sort of ramble is inherently hilarious.”

She also talked about the only interview that ever went south, with the guest ending the conversation after three questions. “Sometimes the universe has different plans for us,” she said when asked why the interview ended.

“It’s an energy thing,” she said. “I think of this as scene work, and these are my scene partners, and so we’re really catching a vibe together. And so I go into it comedy-first. Obviously, the questions and the journalism are part of the entree, but the amuse-bouche is that we are laughing and enjoying ourselves.”

highlights.title: Valve’s Steam Frame costs $1,059
highlights.summary: Valve is finally releasing its Steam Frame headset, which can run both flat and VR games locally and stream both kinds of games from your PC. The Steam Frame will start at $1,059. Valve will also offer a 1TB model that starts at $1,299.
body: You can now register your interest to buy Valve’s new VR headset.

Every Steam Frame will come with a copy of Half-Life: Alyx, Valve’s made-for-VR entry in the Half-Life franchise, and Valve has ported the game to run natively on the headset as well as via streaming.

If you’re chosen in the lottery, Valve should let you purchase on September 18th. If not, you can still join the waitlist. Once you get an offer to purchase a Steam Frame, you’ll have 72 hours to complete your order.

If you want the least pressure on your face, my colleague Sean Hollister, who reviewed the headset, strongly recommends Valve’s ergonomic accessories kit, which comes with a removable top head strap that really helps the 1-pound headset float more comfortably, as well as a nose piece that blocks out more light for better immersion and a pair of “Knuckles”-style hand straps that can let you fully open and close your hands in VR games without dropping the controllers.

highlights.title: How Fyxer built an AI executive assistant people trust
highlights.summary: Fyxer uses OpenAI models, fine-tuning, memory, and real user feedback to organize inboxes and draft emails in each user’s voice.
body: Fyxer pairs OpenAI models with 500,000+ hours of EA workflows and real user feedback to draft replies in each person’s voice.

For many professionals, work means keeping track of conversations and commitments across inboxes, meetings, messages, and apps. Without rock-solid context, those commitments can fall through the cracks, damaging projects and relationships.

Fyxer built an AI executive assistant that follows the thread as work moves across tools. It combines the latest OpenAI models with more than 500,000 hours of executive assistant workflows, dividing the work among dozens of specialized models that improve through real user feedback.

Email is one of the clearest places to see it in action. Two people can receive the same email and need completely different replies depending on the relationship, what has happened before, and what each person is trying to get done. That makes a seemingly simple task deceptively hard for AI.

body: The multi-project deal supposedly begins with a feature-film adaptation of Crazy Taxi, Sega's long-running series of whacky arcade racing games that's being revived soon, penned by the screenwriting duo responsible for last year's The Naked Gun reboot (Dan Gregor and Doug Mand). The producers behind the surprisingly good live-action Sonic films (Neal H. Moritz, Toby Ascher, and Sega's Toru Nakahara) are also involved with this one, per Variety. No telling if it'll be animated or live-action, though.

On the flip side, the Sonic Netflix series is set to be an animated romp that, according to Sega, is "high-voltage, comedic, yet emotionally grounded" and is "built for kids who want to feel a little edge, a little attitude, and a lot of 'that's my crew' wish fulfillment." Expect to see lots of the extended anthropomorphic Sonic family, then. Nakahara and animation director Carlos Stevens are attached.

And, finally, we have a film adaptation of Stranger Than Heaven also planned. RGG Studio's crime-ridden action game isn't due to come out until next year, 15 January, but Sega's giving it the multimedia treatment early.

highlights.title: Valve has ported Half-Life: Alyx to ARM, and it’s free with Steam Frame
highlights.summary: Today, Valve is launching its first headset since 2019 - the new Steam Frame - while dodging our questions about whether it'll ever make another VR game to go with it. But buyers of the $1,059 gadget will get one flagship VR game anyhow, and it's great.
body: One of the best PC VR games now runs natively on a Qualcomm Snapdragon chip.

Every Steam Frame comes with a copy of 2020’s Half-Life: Alyx, one of the best VR games yet made and a good game, period, and you won’t even need a desktop PC — because Valve has ported the entire game to ARM64 so it can run natively on the Frame’s Qualcomm Snapdragon Gen 3 chip.

That’s no mean feat: This was a game that required a VR-ready Windows desktop or laptop with a midrange graphics card back in 2020, now running on what’s effectively souped-up smartphone silicon. It even supports all the mods and extra levels that fans have built! My mods and saves were waiting for me the moment I fired it up.

The port certainly has compromises in graphical fidelity compared to running it on my desktop, but it manages to feel like a full PC VR game on the Frame in a way that native Meta Quest titles never really have, and without removing any objects or assets. Typically, standalone VR games feel emptier.

highlights.title: Fashion app Daydream uses Apple Intelligence to help you shop the outfits in your camera roll
highlights.summary: Thanks to the launch of iOS 27, Daydream's app now includes features that can turn saved outfit photos into shoppable results and search for products through Siri without opening the app.
body: Daydream, an AI-powered fashion discovery app, launched two new features on Monday to let iPhone users turn saved outfit photos into shoppable results and search for clothing and accessories through Siri, without opening the app.

The new features were built using Apple’s iOS 27 developer tools, which officially rolled out today. To use either feature, you’ll need an iPhone running iOS 27 with Siri AI enabled, along with the Daydream app installed. The app is free to download on iOS devices.

The first feature uses Apple’s image-context capabilities, letting users shop from images already saved in their Photos app. Daydream analyzes the outfit in the image, identifies its individual pieces, and automatically surfaces shoppable matches and similar styles from Daydream’s catalog of roughly 3 million products.

highlights.title: AI Leaders Are Calling for a Slowdown. Trump’s Team Says It’s on Them
highlights.summary: Sam Altman and Elon Musk backed Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s weekend plea for regulation. The White House seems unlikely to oblige.
body: As calls for artificial intelligence regulation intensify, US President Donald Trump’s team have made it clear that if lab leaders want to implement an industry-wide slowdown, they’re going to have to do it themselves.

Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called on the US government to regulate AI companies within a wider effort to slow the pace of the technology’s development in an essay published Saturday. The essay received rare endorsement from both OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman and Elon Musk, who owns chatbot Grok, following a week of intense debate about the technology’s threats to human safety. Microsoft chief executive officer Satya Nadella also called for pacing development.

Calls for AI slowdown and regulation have intensified after a number of researchers voiced major concerns in the last week about the speed of the technology’s advance. “AI progress is increasing,” former DeepMind researcher Rishub Jain told WIRED. “And as AI becomes more capable, it poses more risks.”

For Gray, a veteran of Edinburgh derbies as a player and head coach, not forgetting his winning goal for Hibs in the 2016 Scottish Cup final against Rangers, it is "a brilliant opportunity" and one that has "a bit more spice to it" because of the opposition.
For Vrancken, who joined Hearts from his hometown club of Sint-Truiden this summer, it will simply be "nice for the fans" to be facing their bitter rivals.

body: Across 17 initial reviews, Rotten Tomatoes has Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother sitting at a perfect 100%. It's not just certified fresh, it's a certified masterpiece. The film follows Ali as a religiously devout hitman who fights his way across Houston to protect his children following the death of his wife. The action is especially impressive and reflects Ali's preparation for Blade. Ali is joined by a cast that includes John Cho, Giancarlo Esposito, and Tramell Tillman, among others.

Praise is universally given to Ali's performance and the overall aesthetic of the film. Zachary Lee at TheWrap wrote that "what Ali, Tariq and the collaborators have assembled feels not just like kismet but divinely ordained, as if this was the movie they were always meant to make." While Ali and Tariq's Blade will always remain a " what if? ", audiences will be happy that something as good as Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother came out of it.

I bought my house in my late 20s, with minimal home-maintenance knowledge, a flathead screwdriver, a rubber mallet that had lived through the Carter administration – and the realization that throughout my life, I had been spared from doing the dirty work at the cost of learning how it was done.

I cobbled my education together from online tutorials, Reddit threads and a lot of trial and error.

highlights.title: New York Seizes a Dozen Celebrity Deepfake Websites
highlights.summary: In the biggest-ever legal action against harmful deepfake websites, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office has seized 12 sites that collectively targeted around 1,200 victims.
body: For the best part of a decade, abusive deepfake “pornography” websites have published thousands of nonconsensual videos depicting women, including high-profile celebrities, politicians, and public figures, into sexual situations. Now, in what is likely the largest takedown of explicit deepfake websites to date, officials in New York have seized more than a dozen of the harmful sites.

On Monday, the Manhattan District Attorney’s Office announced the seizure of 12 domains which it says have been used for “unlawfully” sharing, publishing, and selling celebrity deepfake videos. Around 1,200 people—overwhelmingly women—were depicted in nonconsensual sexual images and videos on the websites, the office says. These included social media influencers, actors, activists, athletes, musicians, and politicians.

highlights.title: ‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisis | Sid Lowe
highlights.summary: The World Cup winner’s off-the-cuff assessment was brutally honest. Within days their manager and CEO were gone, but the problems run much deeper. Kiat Lim wanted to see Valencia play so badly, so that is what he did.
body: Above him as he went in were giant portraits of Mario Kempes, Antonio Puchades, Juan Sol, Gaizka Mendieta, David Villa and Santiago Cañizares, footballers from a better time; around him were yellow banners and whistles for the footballers there now. Inside, Lim saw the game start with the lower south stand empty as fans stayed away until the 19th minute, the sound of another protest drifting in from the street. They were out there still when, sitting alongside Joan Laporta, he saw Lamine Yamal score the sixth-minute opener then get a second. And although that, also from Lamine Yamal, was ruled out, he eventually saw Barcelona get four more, presiding over a 5-0 debut defeat.

He had seen supporters leave early, seen those that stayed turn towards him, chanting for him and his family to leave for good. He had seen the hankies come out and his players head into the tunnel heads bowed. He heard his manager insist that they were hurt but not sunk. What he did not see – what no one had seen yet but everyone would see soon enough – was the verdict from the bench.

highlights.title: Sexually Explicit Deepfake Sites Target 100-Plus Politicians in Europe
highlights.summary: An analysis of 160 deepfake websites reveals politicians in 22 countries appear on them. Nearly all of them are women.
body: Almost 150 politicians across Europe have been included on harmful deepfake pornography websites over the last few years, according to new research seen by WIRED. Some of the politicians, who are overwhelmingly women, have had their likeness included in explicit videos, while others have names and photos listed in disturbing database-like entries that can link to deepfake creation tools.

Analysis of around 160 domains that host deepfake abuse and other nonconsensual sexual content, by researcher Benjamin Shultz, has found that at least 138 women members of parliament (MPs) from 22 European Union countries have appeared or been mentioned on the sites. In contrast, only nine male MPs were referenced in any way. By Shultz’s calculations, it is 33 times more likely for women MPs to be targeted by deepfake ecosystems.

highlights.title: Wardogs Players Really Want You To Close The Doors … Or Else
highlights.summary: The hottest game on PC right now is Wardogs, the Battlefield-like mass multiplayer FPS by developer Bulkhead that's soaring up the Steam charts. While it may not be as hot as the game itself, the game's subreddit is full of hotheads demanding you do one teeny-tiny thing. Close. The. Doors. Behind.
body: Released in a closed beta state in August 2026 before entering early access in September 2026, Wardogs has taken PC gaming by storm. It's not only the number-one trending game according to SteamDB, with an all-time peak of 428,666 concurrent players on September 13, but it's also the fourth-most-played game on Steam, trailing behind Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, and PUBG: Battlegrounds. Folks can't get enough of being a dog of war.
Something folks would love to get enough of, though? Players leaving those gosh-darn doors and gates open when venturing out onto the battlefield.

All over the official Wardogs subreddit are a ton of players decrying the carelessness of other players when it comes to not closing doors and gates behind them. Redditor demonmit1 posted on September 14, pleading for people to stop building so many gates and close the ones they open.

"If you're helping build a FOB, please… We only need one air locked gate for logistics," demonmit1 said. "No one closes them anyways, so adding more is not good. Stop it. If someone wants to leave the base, they can jump over a wall. They don't need to leave through a door they'll forget to close."
